transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling cardholder services. My name is Marcus. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Hi Marcus, yeah, my name is Owen Taggart. I'm calling because I paid for some concert tickets and I never actually got them.
Agent: I can look into that for you, Mr. Taggart. First, could you please verify your billing zip code and the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Sure, the zip code is 80204, and the card ends in 1184.
Agent: Thank you. I have your account pulled up. Can you tell me the name of the company and when you made the purchase?
Customer: It was StagePass Tix, and I placed the order back on September 17th.
Agent: I see that transaction on September 17th. How were the tickets supposed to be delivered to you?
Customer: When I checked out, it said they'd send them over either by email as an electronic pass or in the mail, but I never got an email or anything in my physical mailbox.
Agent: Did you happen to check your spam or junk email folder around that time?
Customer: Yeah, I checked spam, deleted items, everywhere. There was nothing from them.
Agent: Have you tried getting in touch with StagePass Tix directly about this?
Customer: I sent two messages through their website contact form, but nobody ever wrote me back.
Agent: Understood. When was the concert scheduled to take place?
Customer: It was last Saturday, October 10th. So the concert has already happened, and we couldn't even go.
Agent: And how many tickets were included in that purchase?
Customer: It was two tickets, one for me and one for my brother.
Agent: Did the seller ever provide you with a confirmation number or tracking link when you checked out?
Customer: There was an order number on the screen when I finished paying, but that was it. No link to print anything, and no barcodes ever came through.
Agent: Let me make sure I have everything noted correctly. On September 17th, you bought two concert tickets from StagePass Tix, you never received them electronically or by mail, the seller didn't respond to your messages, and the event has already passed.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
